description: Canonical provider cost and per-query pricing for the people/company search generators. Source of truth for credit metering. All rates are the rates Arxena actually pays (no free tier assumed). Customer billing is per provider event at a 1.25 margin.

creditModel.granularityNote: Every billable provider event is charged on its own. Bundles in referenceBundles are display aggregations only and are never the charged unit.
creditModel.calculationRule: chargedMicroCredits = round(usdPerUnit * marginMultiplier * 1000000), rounded half-up in a single step from the USD rate. Do not re-round the at-cost micro-credit figure and then multiply.

assumptions.freeTierNote: No free-tier allocation is counted for Arxena. Every provider request is a cost.
assumptions.cacheNote: ProviderQueryCacheService dedupes SERP responses, Business Search pages and dataset snapshots. A cache hit costs $0 at the provider and is charged 0.

brightDataSerp.label: Bright Data SERP API
notes: Failed or errored requests are not billed, and therefore must not be charged to the customer.
Async mode bills the submit and not the collect.
Parsing, unlocking, CAPTCHA and internal retries are included.
Custom headers or cookies on a zone switches the zone to bill-all-requests; do not enable them.

brightDataBusinessSearch.label: Bright Data Business Search
notes: Billed per search block on the limit requested, not on rows returned.
A partially filled page still bills a whole block.
A zero-match search that ran is billable, so it must also be charged: charge per search that ran, not per search that returned rows.
Each page of a paginated search is a separate billable search.
The view parameter does not change the price.

brightDataScraper.label: Bright Data Scraper API (LinkedIn profile)
notes: Billed per successfully delivered record; failed deliveries are not billed and must not be charged.
Field count does not change the price.

harvestApi.label: HarvestAPI

contractedRates.note: Contracted basis is the published rate: $0.10 for a whole lead-search page (up to 25 leads) and $0.004 for one individual profile fetched by URL via /linkedin/profile. The full-profile ($0.0064) and profile-with-email ($0.02) rates exist and are catalogued, but the default enrichment path uses the $0.004 profile.

usedFor: Harvest / Sales Navigator equivalent lead search
notes: Lead search pages return up to 25 short leads; a partially filled page bills the same $0.10.
Credits are pay-as-you-go and expire one year after top-up, so unused credit is a real loss.
Discounts apply to the whole top-up package, not to a single call.

unipile.label: Unipile (LinkedIn / Sales Navigator / Recruiter / Premium access)
notes: Derived: $5.00 per month / (10 requests/day * 30 days) = $0.0166666667 per request.
The daily cap is the binding constraint, not the price: 1,000 requests takes about 100 calendar days.
Per-request cost is 11x a Bright Data SERP request. Do not route people search through it; use it only where a real LinkedIn identity is required.
If the underlying subscription lapses, the derived per-request cost is invalid.

elasticsearch.label: Elasticsearch (Arxena company index)
usedFor: company index lookup and org-chart resolution
notes: Priced at $2 per 1,000 requests.
One logical company lookup may issue more than one HTTP search request (variants, retries, multi-search); meter HTTP requests, not logical lookups.
Company index lookups are currently unbilled.

meters.note: Bills at the SERP rate, not a premium rate.

meters.billOn: every search that ran, including zero-match and partial pages
meters.note: Charge per page, never per returned row.
The contracted individual-profile rate: one /linkedin/profile fetch by URL.
20833 = round(0.0166666667 * 1.25 * 1e6). Deliberately not derived from the rounded at-cost 16667, which would give 20834.

googleSerpCompanySweep.description: find_people_by_company Google SERP route: one organic query per role plus boolean/company/site groups, then the AI-Overview question pass.

eventCount.typicalAssumption: 11 of 12 organic queries issued plus one attempt per AI-Overview question

brightDataPeopleCompany.description: find_people_by_company Bright Data route: one natural-language prompt per role variant, planned into shards; each shard samples then pages, and each cell also runs the instant engine.

eventCount.typicalAssumption: 3 role cells x (1 estimate + 1 page + 2 instant)

harvestCompanyOrgChart.description: Harvest lead-search pagination for one company, optionally enriched with Harvest profiles.

elasticsearchCompanyLookup.description: Company index lookup in the Arxena index. Charged per HTTP search request, with no assumed 1:1 relationship to a logical lookup.
elasticsearchCompanyLookup.note: Every search request sent is charged, so a lookup that fans out is not free. At 10 requests a single lookup costs more than a whole 14-event SERP sweep, which makes request count per lookup an efficiency target, not just a metering detail.

costPerThousandPeople.derivation: 1000 / 100 rows per search = 10 searches x BD_SEARCH_PAGE
costPerThousandPeople.coverage: search result rows only, no full profile

costPerThousandPeople.caveat: Capacity-bound: 10 requests/day means 1,000 requests needs about 100 days.

costPerThousandPeople.derivation: priced per company lookup, not per person

referenceBundles.note: NOT charged. Billing is per provider event. These are the sums a customer will see for a typical run at the 1.25 margin, used for display aggregation and for forecasting only.

bundles.label: Company people sweep, Bright Data route (typical)

billingAudit.summary: Only two of the six providers are metered today, and the one metered per record is over-charged 100x while everything else is free to the workspace.

metered.defect: Bills per returned row but the provider bills per search block. A full 100-row page costs $0.002 and is charged $0.20, a 100x over-charge.
metered.fix: Meter BD_SEARCH_PAGE per page using the executor's limit, not per row.

metered.defect: Correct unit, but only company news uses it.
Outside the scope of this catalog.

unmetered.spend: find_people_by_company organic sweep, up to 12 requests per company
AI-Overview question pass, up to 9 requests per company
instant engine inside find_people_by_company, which calls BrightDataBusinessSearchService directly and bypasses billing
company index lookup and org-chart resolution
unmetered.note: Charged on every HTTP search request; request count per lookup is unmeasured and is the open cost driver.

implementationNotes: Meter the event, charge the event: one credit record per provider call, carrying meterId, provider, quantity and unit.
Replace costForRecordsUsd with a per-page unit; the ludicrous executor already knows its page limit, so quantity = pages.
Route find_people_by_company's instant calls through BrightDataBillingService so they are no longer free.
Meter the SERP sweep and the AI-Overview pass inside find-people-google-search.service.ts.
Charge 0 for a cache hit; ProviderQueryCacheService already dedupes SERP responses and Business Search pages.
Never charge a failed provider request, since the provider does not bill it.
Aggregate per-event charges per tool call for display only; the ledger keeps the individual events.
resolvedGaps: Margin multiplier is 1.25 on provider cost.
Billing granularity is per provider event, not per bundle.
AI-Overview zone bills at the SERP rate ($1.50/1K).
No free-tier allocation is counted; all rates are marginal cost.
Elasticsearch is metered at $2 per 1,000 requests, charged on every request with no assumed requests-per-lookup.
LinkedIn-native access is priced from the Unipile $5/month, 10 requests/day subscription rather than a Sales Navigator seat.
Harvest contracted rate is the published rate: $0.10 per whole lead-search page, $0.004 per individual profile.

openQuestions.question: What are the observed averages for queries per company, shards per company, Harvest page fill rate and cache hit rate?
openQuestions.impact: Converts unit prices into real per-run and per-workspace cost, and cache rate is the cheapest lever on the bill.

openQuestions.question: What is the observed request count per company lookup, now that every request is charged?
openQuestions.impact: Pure cost driver with no rate to negotiate: 1 request is $0.0025, 10 requests is $0.025 and exceeds a whole SERP sweep.

openQuestions.question: Can the Unipile cap be raised, or is 10 requests/day hard?
openQuestions.impact: Whether Unipile can serve any batch workload at all.

openQuestions.question: Should the 1.25 margin apply to the Unipile subscription, given it is a fixed monthly cost that may go unused?
openQuestions.impact: At 10 requests/day the full $5 is only recovered if the cap is actually consumed; otherwise the derived per-request cost under-recovers.
